sentiment.label: neutral

Tuttavia, il petrolio in calo (-6.23%) e la situazione geopolitica (guerra tra USA-Israele e Iran) potrebbero influenzare negativamente il mercato. However, declining oil prices (-6.23%) and geopolitical tensions (US-Israel and Iran war) could negatively impact the market. ECB keeps rates unchanged at 2.00% (DFR) and 2.15% (Refi).

Gold gains 0.59% to $4527.00/oz. Oil sharply declines (-6.23%) to $93.38. Global M2 liquidity continues to expand (+4.7% YoY).

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.01%, Shanghai in calo dell'1.25%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

L'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.61%, il VIX è in calo dello 0.24%. L'oro è in rialzo dello 0.59% a 4527 dollari l'oncia. Il petrolio è in calo del 6.23% a 93.38 dollari. Il rendimento del decennale americano è in calo dell'1.43% al 4.49%. Il BTP 10Y è stabile al 3.73%.

Top policymakers della BCE stanno gettando le basi per un aumento dei tassi a giugno. Inoltre, un protrarsi della guerra in Iran potrebbe scatenare una serie di aumenti dei tassi negli Stati Uniti, secondo il Fed's Kashkari.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 
  Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i settantacinque mila dollari, ma registra una lieve flessione dell'uno virgola diciotto percento. 
  I flussi degli ETF mostrano un deflusso di circa centocinque milioni di dollari. 
  Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle prese di profitto degli investitori in attesa di nuovi sviluppi nel mercato.

  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum scende dello zero virgola cinquantanove percento a duemilatre dollari, Solana perde lo stesso valore a ottantatre virgola novantuno dollari, mentre BNB cede lo zero virgola cinquantasei percento a seicentocinquantadue virgola settantasei dollari.

  Il Fear & Greed Index è a venticinque, in zona di Extreme Fear, il che suggerisce cautela tra gli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 0.01%, while Shanghai fell 1.25%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets. The S&P 500 closed up 0.61%, and the VIX is down 0.24%. Gold is up 0.59% at $4,527 per ounce. Oil is down 6.23% at $93.38 The 10-year US yield is down 1.43% at 4.49%. The 10Y BTP is essentially flat at 3.73%. Top ECB policymakers are laying the groundwork for a rate hike in June. Moreover, a prolonged war in Iran could trigger a series of rate hikes in the US, according to the Fed's Kashkari. No major macroeconomic data is due today. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin is holding above $75,000 but is slightly down 1.18%. ETF flows show an outflow of around $105 million. This movement could be influenced by investors taking profits while waiting for new market developments. Among altcoins, Ethereum is down 0.59% at $2,303, Solana loses the same value at $83.91, while BNB drops 0.56% to $652.76 The Fear & Greed Index is at 25, in the Extreme Fear zone, suggesting caution among investors. No macroeconomic data is on the agenda today. For a deeper dive into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Disciplining digital risk: evidence from cyber stress tests
articles.snippet: by Nordine Abidi, Leonardo Gambacorta, Christoffer Kok, Leonardo Madio, Ixart Miquel-Flores, Alberto Partida Investment in cybersecurity in an interconnected banking system has public-good properties: positive externalities can generate systemic underinvestment. Using confidential supervisory data from the European Central Bank, we first identify "laggard" European banks that underinvest relative to their cyber-risk profiles, and then examine how supervisory scrutiny affects their incentives to invest.
articles.title_it: La disciplina del rischio digitale: prove dai test di stress cyber
articles.title_en: Disciplining digital risk: evidence from cyber stress tests
articles.summary_it: Il BIS pubblica un rapporto sulla gestione del rischio digitale nelle banche, evidenziando l'importanza degli investimenti in cybersecurity.
articles.summary_en: The BIS publishes a report on digital risk management in banks, highlighting the importance of cybersecurity investments.

articles.title: Can the Climate Crisis Unite Europe?
articles.snippet: The foundations of Europe’s postwar peace and prosperity are beginning to fracture, yet the European Union still struggles to unite its increasingly divided member states around a common political project. The escalating climate crisis could provide the continent with the shared purpose it has long lacked.

articles.title: American Decline on Display
articles.snippet: Donald Trump’s state visit to Beijing has further demonstrated the relative weakness of the United States and the West vis-à-vis the People’s Republic of China and the Global South. articles.title: U.S. Sends Rare SPR Oil Cargo to Asia as Hormuz Crisis Reshapes Trade
articles.snippet: A tanker loaded with crude oil from the U.S. strategic petroleum reserve has set off from the Gulf of Mexico to the Philippines in what is the first U.S. oil shipment to Asia since late 2022, Reuters reported, citing shipping data. The rare move yet again highlights the rearrangement of energy flows resulting from the shutdown of normal tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran and the United States. Prior to the war, Asia got as much as 80% of its crude oil from the Middle East, the report noted, with the Philippines specifically importing…

articles.title: India Turns to Russia, Brazil, and Venezuela for Crude
articles.snippet: The world’s third-largest crude importer, India, is accelerating efforts to diversify its oil imports in the wake of the Middle East crisis. India had begun raising imports from Russia three years before the Iran war cut off most supplies from the Middle East, on which India relies for about half of its crude purchases. With the Strait of Hormuz de facto closed and only a handful of tankers moving out of the chokepoint per week, and few of these India-bound, the country is looking further away for sources of crude. Africa and South America…
